THE THIRD REVIEW OF 1.24.30 (the lift station: AI_CONTROL's alternating relay and pump-down floats, AI_PUMP_STATION's
MAKE PIPING and MAKE LEVELS, AI_PARTS's questions in parts). Reviewed at faaf132 by a reviewer that did not write the
rules and did not read the first two reviews' cases or tests/liftstation.js.

HOW TO REPLAY
  node tests/fixtures/liftstation_review3_1230/replay.js            (A, B, C, D, F: jsdom, about 2 s)
  python3 tools/build_site.py
  python3 tests/fixtures/liftstation_review3_1230/replay_browser.py (E: Chromium, port 8339; PNGs to $LANTERN_PNG_OUT
                                                                     or png/ beside it)
  node tests/fixtures/liftstation_review3_1230/make_before.js       (remakes before.json, 1.24.29's drawings of the
                                                                     A cases, from git show lantern-1.24.29)
  load.js and sim.js are copies of the second review's harness (read and checked before use); lib.js and every case
  are this review's own.

COUNTS
  jsdom (replay.js):            272 cases: 223 AGREE, 49 DISAGREE
    A over-reach        54 cases,  8 DISAGREE (8 medium)
    B small models      74 cases, 17 DISAGREE (1 high, 8 medium, 8 low)
    C Chat end to end   33 cases,  5 DISAGREE (2 medium, 3 low)
    D splitting         87 cases, 12 DISAGREE (7 medium, 5 low)
    F truth             24 cases,  7 DISAGREE (2 medium, 5 low)
  Chromium (replay_browser.py):  16 cases: 15 AGREE, 1 DISAGREE (1 medium)
  In all:                       288 cases: 238 AGREE, 50 DISAGREE (1 high, 28 medium, 21 low), in 20 root causes

  Against 1.24.29 (A): of the 54 plain circuits, 46 are drawn as 1.24.29 drew them or better (the pump-down rule
  mends 8 sump/pit/drain circuits that 1.24.29 short-cycled: A-08, A-09, A-10, A-17, A-30, A-31, A-48, A-49); 8 are
  worse (A-11, A-15, A-16, A-36: a fill rewired as a pump-down; A-33, A-34, A-35, A-51: sent back for an alternator
  the question did not ask for). One benign difference: the list of what MAKE CONTROL draws now ends ", alternator".

  The standards the summaries cite were read on their pages by this reviewer (2026-11-20) and say what Lantern says:
  Recommended Standards for Wastewater Facilities 2014 (Ohio EPA's copy, dam.assets.ohio.gov/.../10wastewaterstandards
  -2014.pdf): 42.52 "Suitable shutoff and check valves shall be placed on the discharge line of each pump ... The check
  valve shall be located between the shutoff valve and the pump."; 44.4 "Valves required under Paragraph 42.5 shall be
  located in a separate valve chamber."; 42.64 "Covered wet wells shall have provisions for air displacement to the
  atmosphere, such as an inverted "j" tube or other means." Ontario, Design Guidelines for Sewage Works 2008, 7.2.5
  Controls (ontario.ca): "Float controls should be at least 300 mm (12 in) vertically and 450 mm (18 in) horizontally
  apart". (The health.mn.gov copy of Ten States would not open.)

WHAT HELD (selected AGREEs)
  - The duplex: the instructions' example, and 30-odd small-model variants of it (no quotes, "= off", "FS1: off float",
    bullets, numbered lines, lower case, P1/P2, K1/K2 contactors, "alternator relay", "alternating", a relay labelled
    "alternating relay", floats written on the pumps, alarm light on the alternator, fault lights on overloads, HOA and
    thermal switches, a system on/off relay) simulated: lead call held to the off float, the pumps take turns, the lag
    float runs both, the alarm lights at its float, an overload drops only its pump. The 35B's own two blocks too.
  - Every statement in the duplex summary is true of the simulated ladder (F-01..F-03, after a fresh power-up: M1 leads
    first, as the steps say).
  - MAKE LEVELS reads 2ft, 2', 2 ft 6 in, 3'-6", 4 ft-6 in, 5'6", 0.6 m, 0,6 m, 600 mm, 1,000 mm, 60 cm, depths below
    grade in a well of given depth, elevations with the floor's; draws them to scale (measured); the 300 mm note is
    right at 299, 300 and 304.8 mm.
  - MAKE PIPING: check before shutoff on every pump, the summary's valve names are the plan's and the drawing's order;
    force-main valves, air release, missing pumps for "two pump"/"duplex", floats left to MAKE LEVELS.
  - AI_PARTS: 50 one-thing questions across the suite ("and", "plus", "as well as", "1 ft 6 in", "2.5 m", "3,000 psi",
    "step 1.", colons, "the first verse", "1st float") are not split; no bench question but make-liftstation and
    make-liftstation-b splits (both sets); 22 multi-part questions split right.
  - Chat and the bench's path: all blocks at once (1 call), wrong order, prose twice for a later part, a later part
    wrong twice, the control again and again, MAKE DRAWING for the levels: each part made once, a part not made said,
    never said made, the turn ends, nothing asked for more than twice.
  - Drawings in Chromium (16, full size and as the model sees them): no text on text, nothing cut off, no label through
    a line, except E-11 (below).

DISAGREEMENTS, BY ROOT CAUSE, HIGHEST HARM FIRST

1. [HIGH] A low-level alarm light is taken for the high-level alarm and put on the alarm float (B-28)
   Input:  the example's duplex plus a right low-level alarm: float FS0 LT4 nc "low level alarm", lamp LT4 "low level
           alarm" amber, lamp LT3 FS4 "high level alarm" red (question: a 2 pump lift station with an alternating relay).
   Lantern: LT4's rung becomes FS4 (high level alarm, open) in series with FS0 (closed): it can never light (it needs the
           water above the high alarm and below the low float at once). Nothing is said. Without LT3, the only light on
           the high-level alarm is the amber one labelled "low level alarm".
   Right:  a light that says "low" is not the high-level alarm's; left as written.
   Where:  AI_CONTROL circuit(), takeTurns: var ALARM = /\balarm|high[\s-]*(level|water)|flood|overflow/i (line 33913)
           matches "low level alarm"; the switch loop then adds FS0 to the same rung (its refs were never cleared, the
           low float being left out of allF).

2. [MEDIUM] The pump-down rule ignores the question: a fill becomes a pump that empties (A-11, A-15, A-16, A-36)
   Input:  "Draw the control circuit for a pump that fills a water tank, starting at low level and stopping at high
           level": float FS1 M1 "low level", float FS2 M1 "high level", coil M1 "pump starter". Also a well pump that
           fills a storage tank ("low"/"high", coil "well pump"), a transfer pump that fills tank B (floats "tank B
           low"/"tank B high"), a relay "level relay" for a fill.
   Lantern: rewires FS2 (high) as the start and FS1 (low) as the stop with a holding contact, and says "FS2 (high level)
           starts M1 and FS1 (low level) stops it: M1 holds itself in between (the two in series would stop it as soon
           as the water fell below FS2 ...: short-cycling)". For a fill this is a pump that starts when the tank is
           full and never stops (the water it pumps never falls): an overflow, explained as right. 1.24.29 left the
           model's (also wrong) series floats as written.
   Right:  rule 7: act only when the circuit can be nothing else. The question says fill: leave it as written (or back
           once with NC floats for a fill).
   Where:  AI_CONTROL circuit(), lines 34032-34054: the fill test reads only the floats' and the coil's labels
           (/\bfill\w*|.../.test(o.label)); build() has ctx.question but circuit() never sees it.

3. [MEDIUM] Any "alternat..." word is read as asking for an alternating relay (A-33, A-34, A-35, A-51)
   Input:  "two sump pumps that alternate by a manual selector switch, each pump with its own float"; "two sump pumps
           with floats and an alternate power source"; "run on alternate weeks by a selector switch"; "a duplex sewage
           pump station with an alternate (standby) pump that starts on a high float" -- each answered with a right
           circuit (each pump on its own float).
   Lantern: "the question asks for an alternating relay, and this block has none: add the line alternator AR M1 M2 --
           Lantern then wires the floats, the call relays and the pumps itself". A model that obeys gets an automatic
           duplex the person did not ask for. 1.24.29 drew them as written.
   Right:  only "alternating relay", "alternator", "pumps that alternate/take turns automatically" ask for one.
   Where:  AI_CONTROL build(), line 34299: /\balternat\w*/i.test(qq.replace(NO_ALT, " ")) && isPumps(qq).

4. [MEDIUM] Adam's question with the first part answered in prose twice: the turn ends, nothing made, the other two
   parts never asked for (C-08 Chat, C-34 the bench's path)
   Input:  Adam's question; the 35B's own first reply (prose: "I cannot create visual diagrams ...") twice, then the
           piping and levels blocks.
   Lantern: Chat: "The AI explained instead of writing a MAKE CONTROL block; Lantern asked for the block itself...",
           then "From the AI's own knowledge ..." and the turn ends after 2 calls; the piping and the levels are never
           asked for, and nothing says the three were not made. The bench's path: no parts at all (2 calls).
           (A first part whose BLOCK is wrong twice is handled: said, and the second asked for -- C-09.)
   Right:  as for a later part: the first part left and said, the second asked for with its own instructions.
   Where:  AI_PARTS again() and skip() return null when parts.cur is 0 (if (!parts || !parts.cur) return null, lines
           70866-70880), and Chat's no-block ask is once a turn (blockAsked); AI_ACTIONS solve(): parts are split only
           when a block was made (parts = PT && PT.split && made ? ..., line 31055).

5. [MEDIUM] Lines sent back that are wrong for this block (rule 3)
   a. B-02. The example with its float FS4 line left out (lamp LT3 FS4 "high level" kept): "LT3 names FS4, which is
      not drawn: add a line for it, like: coil FS4 "<what it is>" or limit FS4 LT3". FS4 is a float; the line is
      float FS4 "high level alarm" (or Lantern adds it: it already adds an alarm float for a lone alarm light).
      Where: AI_CONTROL circuit(), line 34004 (the message offers coil/limit whatever the tag says).
   b. B-29. A 5-float duplex whose low-level alarm float has no light: "float FS1: name the coil or light it switches,
      like: float FS1 CR1" -- CR1 is the lead call relay Lantern makes; obeyed, it makes CR1 a meaningless relay on the
      low float. Right: give it a light (lamp LT1 FS1 nc "low level alarm"), or add it and say so. Where: line 33987
      (the first coil is suggested).
   c. B-30. The question asks for an alternating relay; the block has the four floats and two pump starters and no
      alternator: 7 problems go back -- each float "like: float FS1 M1", each pump "start PB2 M1" / "coil M1 CR1" --
      and only the last says "add the line alternator AR M1 M2". The six others contradict it; obeyed with it, they
      give the block of finding 6, which Lantern cannot draw. Right: the alternator line alone (Lantern wires the rest).
      Where: build() line 34299-34306 appends to circuit()'s generic problems instead of replacing them.
   d. B-47, B-49, B-50. MAKE LEVELS sends the instructions' example heights whatever the block's: for a block at 2, 3,
      4, 5 ft with two "lead on" floats: "two floats for lead on (FS2 and FS3): one float each, like: float FS1 "off" 2
      ft, float FS2 "lead on" 3.5 ft, float FS3 "lag on" 4.5 ft, float FS4 "high level alarm" 5.5 ft"; for a block in
      metres with FS3's height left out, the same feet; for "FS1: off float at 2 ft" lines (which MAKE CONTROL reads),
      "not a line of MAKE LEVELS ... like: ... 3.5 ft ...". A small model copies 3.5/4.5/5.5 ft. Right: this block's own
      heights and unit (float FS3 "lag on" 4 ft). Where: planLevels' WRITE (line 34801), used in four messages.
   e. B-81. "MAKE SCHEMATIC" (the word in "plumbing schematic") holding piping lines, for a plumbing question: back
      with the hydraulic reader's problems ("is not a part Lantern draws (it draws: pump, relief, cylinder ...)", "there
      is no cylinder") and its guide; MAKE PIPING is never named. Right: built as piping, or back with "write MAKE
      PIPING". Where: AI_PUMP_STATION hooks the schematic action's match only, not its build/fixHint.

6. [MEDIUM] A duplex with a start button on a pump goes back with Lantern's own failure and no line (B-31)
   Input:  the example with the hint's own first two lines copied in: stop PB1 M1, start PB2 M1 (the lines a small
           model sees first in the pump-station instructions).
   Lantern: "Lantern could not draw this circuit correctly (M1's holding contact is not across its start)".
   Right:  drawn (a hand start beside the duplex) or back once with the line ("leave start PB2 M1 out: with an
           alternator the floats start the pumps").
   Where:  AI_CONTROL circuit(): the duplex gives each pump rung branches (line 33963), the switch loop still puts PB2
           in its starts (33994) and the latching loop sets seal; layout() draws the branches instead of the start and
           its holding contact (34156), so verify() (34264) fails.

7. [MEDIUM] AI_PARTS: a later part without a "thing" word is folded into the part before (D-74, D-83, D-84, D-86, D-90)
   Input:  "Can you draw me the control circuit for a two pump lift station with an alternating relay, then the plumbing
           for the same, and then where the floats go?"; "..., then the plumbing for the same, then where the floats
           go"; "..., then the plumbing, and show where the floats should be set"; "Draw the control circuit for a
           duplex lift station. Then show where the floats hang in the wet well."; "Draw the control for a duplex
           sewage lift station, the force main and valves, and the float settings".
   Lantern: 2 parts, the levels (or the piping) made a detail of the part before: {the plumbing for the same, and then
           where the floats go}; {Draw the control ..., the force main and valves}; the fourth not split at all (both
           tools offered at once). The float levels (or the piping) are never asked for, and nothing says so.
   Right:  CONTROL | PIPING | LEVELS (asksLevels itself reads "where ... floats ... go/set/hang"; asksPiping reads "the
           force main and valves").
   Where:  AI_PARTS pieces(): a later piece is a head only with VERB && THING (line 70720); a detail piece is never
           tried against relevant(); "the force main and valves" is cut at "and" before the piping is recognised.

8. [MEDIUM] AI_PARTS: a part's second tool blocks a later part of that tool (D-76)
   Input:  "Make a table of the float heights for a duplex lift station and draw the float levels".
   Lantern: not split; both MAKE SHEET and MAKE LEVELS offered as one; the drawing is not asked for.
   Right:  SHEET | LEVELS.
   Where:  split(): part 1's acts are [levels, sheet] (PREFER puts SHEET first), and used() (line 70760) counts every
           act of a part, so "draw the float levels" finds no tool "not yet taken" and becomes a detail.

9. [MEDIUM] AI_PARTS: "a chart of the pump cycles" becomes a MAKE SCHEMATIC part (D-77)
   Input:  "Make a spreadsheet of float levels and a chart of the pump cycles".
   Lantern: SHEET | SCHEMATIC{a chart of the pump cycles} (the word "pump" routes to the electrical schematic).
   Right:  one SHEET (a chart is a sheet's), or SHEET | SHEET.
   Where:  PREFER (line 70688) has no chart -> SHEET.

10. [MEDIUM] MAKE LEVELS: a well's rim elevation squashes the floats onto the floor (F-14, E-11)
   Input:  well "wet well" rim el. 110.0 ft, float FS1 "off" el. 101.5 ft ... FS4 "high level alarm" el. 104.5 ft.
   Lantern: the floats are drawn 5, 9, 13 and 18 px above the floor of a 460 px well, their lines through the pumps
           (46 px high); the drawing is presented as to scale. (PNG: png/E-11.png.)
   Right:  the rim is at el. 110.0: the floats drawn on the same scale in the lower part of a ~10 ft well, or back
           for the floor's elevation.
   Where:  planLevels, line 34826: with elevations the floats and inlets get -= base, the well does not; layoutLevels,
           line 34850, takes c.well.h.m (110 ft) as the well's depth.

11. [MEDIUM] MAKE LEVELS: an inlet invert written after the pipe's size in its quotes is dropped, and the summary says
    it is above the floats (F-15)
   Input:  floats at 2, 3, 4, 5 ft; inlet "8 in gravity sewer at 4.5 ft".
   Lantern: no invert height; the inlet drawn above every float; the summary: "...; the inlet's invert above them."
           The note that the alarm (5 ft) is above the invert (4.5 ft) -- the sewer fills before the alarm -- is lost.
           (inlet "inlet invert at 4.5 ft" and an unquoted "inlet 8 in sewer invert 4.5 ft" are read right.)
   Right:  4.5 ft read (heightOf already passes over "8 in gravity"), drawn there, and the alarm note given.
   Where:  parseLevels, line 34772: a quoted label holding a pipe size is skipped whole.

12. [LOW] Numbers outside the quotes land in the floats' labels (B-09, B-35)
   "1. float FS1 "off"" -> FS1 (off 1), FS2 (lead on 2) ...; float FS1 "off" 2 ft in MAKE CONTROL -> "off 2" (the
   unit dropped). Drawn right otherwise. Where: AI_CONTROL parse(), line 33743 (a word with a digit joins the label).

13. [LOW] Heights with no unit are dropped without a word (B-43, B-44)
   float FS1 "off" 2 ... 5, or "el 101.5": drawn in order, "Not to scale: give each float its height above the floor"
   -- the model gave them. Right: back once for the unit, with this block's numbers (float FS1 "off" 2 ft), or say
   they were not read.

14. [LOW] The levels drawing's floor (F-20, F-21, F-24)
   Elevations without the floor's, or depths without the well's: the floor is placed by Lantern (about el. 100.3 ft;
   20.7 ft below grade) and labelled "wet well floor (0)", unsaid. With the floor's elevation given (el. 100.0 ft) it
   is still "(0)" beside floats labelled "el. 101.5 ft"; with depths, "(0)" beside "18 ft below grade" (E-09, E-10).

15. [LOW] Changes made and not said (F-04, B-36, B-34)
   The off float written nc is drawn open (right, unsaid); a horn written with nothing switching it is put on the alarm
   float (right, unsaid); LSHH (an ISA tag of four letters, no number) is drawn and named FS1 ("the high level alarm
   light LT1 on FS1"), unsaid.

16. [LOW] Chat while the first part is still to make (C-10, C-11)
   a. A piping block for part 2 first, then the piping again when the control is asked for: the second is shown and
      counted (rec.mades: PIPING, PIPING, CONTROL, LEVELS) -- the person sees the piping twice. Where: Chat's stray check
      is skipped when askParts.cur is 0 (line 21417).
   b. The piping and the levels in the first reply: the levels block is dropped and asked for again (3 calls, not 2).
      Where: inReply(parts, reply) (line 70888) takes only the part now asked for.

17. [LOW] A part's own words (D-63, D-89, C-16)
   "First, draw the control ...; second, its piping; third, the float positions." -> parts {draw the control ...,
   second} {its piping, third}; "Next,"/"Finally," likewise. "Draw a 2 pump lift station: the control, the plumbing
   and the float positions": the piping request reads "The question also asks for: the plumbing." (the station is in
   the tool's ask, not in the words the model reads).

18. [LOW] Which tools a question gets (D-51, D-52, F-33)
   "the control circuit for a duplex lift station with lead and lag floats and a high level alarm" is offered MAKE
   LEVELS as well as MAKE CONTROL (asksLevels: "floats and a high level"); "a 2.5 m deep wet well ... with the floats
   and the inlet" gets only the picture on the grid; "the plumbing for the sump pump in my basement" gets MAKE PIPING,
   drawn with a valve vault and told the wastewater standard (42.52, 44.4).

19. [LOW] Piping words (B-72, B-73)
   "Force main: 4 in" -> the summary "... and away along the 4 in."; "inlet gate valve" -> an inlet pipe labelled
   "inlet: gate valve", no valve, unsaid.

20. [LOW] Two circuits of one kind in one question (D-91; the same in 1.24.29)
   "Draw a control circuit for a motor ... Then draw a control circuit for a conveyor ..." -> one part; the conveyor's
   is never asked for and nothing says it was not made.

NOT RUN OR NOT CHECKED
  - No real model: every Chat and bench case is a scripted stand-in (the 35B's three recorded replies, and blocks
    written here). Nothing here says how the 0.8B/2B/4B/35B behave.
  - How the drawings look to a person is Adam's to judge; the PNGs are in png/ (full size, and as the model sees them).
    The text checks measure label boxes with the canvas's own font, not the glyphs; a label touching a wire at its
    first letter (E-02, "pump 1 hand-o..." at the branch's wire) is not flagged.
  - The simulator closes every selector, limit, pressure and temperature switch; an open switch's effect (e.g. the
    35B's "lead/lag select" in M1's rung stopping M1's turn) was not simulated.
  - Ten States 44.4 applies to submersible stations; whether a dry-well station's drawing needs a vault was not tried.
